summary: I'll show pizzas before drinks on the menu and add a short line under the shop name saying you deliver within three miles.

personas.label: Customer
personas.description: Browses the menu and orders pizza as a guest.

personas.label: Shop owner
personas.description: Signs in to manage the menu, orders and settings.

stories.goal: see the pizza section before the drinks section when browsing the menu
acceptance: On the home page menu, every pizza item appears above every drink item, regardless of alphabetical order of the category names
Any other category on the menu keeps its current position relative to the other categories

stories.goal: see a short note under the shop name saying delivery is available within three miles
acceptance: A line reading 'We deliver within 3 miles' appears directly under the shop name wherever the shop name is shown to customers

outOfScope: Changing the postcode list or how delivery area is enforced at checkout
Changing menu item data, prices or categories themselves
assumptions: The shop name is shown in the site header on every customer-facing page (the frame around the pages); the delivery line is added directly below it there, not only on the home page.
The exact wording used is 'We deliver within 3 miles'.

The menu currently lists categories alphabetically. I'll keep each category's items in their existing order, but move the category containing pizzas to the top and the category containing drinks to the bottom; any other categories keep their current relative order in between.
This is a display change only: no menu item, price or category data is changed, and no new settings are added for the owner to edit the delivery line or category order later.
